## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to design streaming, approximate matrix products with guarantees, not just recompute.

## Key Concepts
- TensorSketch / random hashing
- Frobenius norm guarantees
- Amortized updates in batches
- Space-time trade-offs vs exact recomputation

## Code Example
```python
# Pseudocode
initialize SA, SD of shape (k, n)
for batch in batches:
  for (i,j,v) in batch:
    SA[:,i] += v * h_j
    SD[j,:] += v * h_i
C_hat = SA.T @ SD
```

- How do sparsity patterns affect accuracy and cost?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical incremental connectivity under batched updates, mirroring real-time systems that accumulate changes before checks. It probes DSU usage, amortized analysis, and how to bound work across batches.

## Key Concepts
- Incremental connectivity with union-find
- Boundary abstraction via virtual nodes
- Amortized analysis under batch processing
- Space-time trade-offs and optimizations

## Code Example
```javascript
// Pseudo: DSU with virtual left/right, mapping (i,j) to id = i*n + j
class DSU { constructor(n){ this.p=new Int32Array(n); this.r=new Int8Array(n); for(let i=0;i<n;i++) this.p[i]=i; } find(x){ while(this.p[x]!=x){ this.p[x]=this.p[this.p[x]]; x=this.p[x]; } return x; } union(a,b){ a=this.find(a); b=this.find(b); if(a==b) return; if(this.r[a]<this.r[b]) [a,b]=[b,a]; this.p[b]=a; if(this.r[a]==this.r[b]) this.r[a]++; } }
```

- How would you adapt for non-grid graphs with higher degree?
- What changes when edges have weights and you ask for connectivity under a threshold?

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to design dynamic range properties with batched updates and amortized analysis, leveraging a segment-tree style approach for real-time run-length maintenance.

## Key Concepts

- Segment tree storing (length, pref1, suf1, best1)
- Merge to propagate cross-boundary runs
- Amortized batch updates vs per-item cost
- Cache-friendly iterative layout

## Code Example

```python
class Node:
    def __init__(self, length=0, pref=0, suf=0, best=0):
        self.length = length
        self.pref = pref
        self.suf = suf
        self.best = best

def merge(a, b):
    length = a.length + b.length
    pref = a.length if a.pref == a.length else a.pref
    if a.pref == a.length:
        pref = a.length + b.pref
    suf = b.length if b.suf == b.length else b.suf
    if b.suf == b.length:
        suf = b.length + a.suf
    best = max(a.best, b.best, a.suf + b.pref)
    return Node(length, pref, suf, best)
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you extend to range flips (set to 0/1) or range updates? 
- How does performance adapt when B approaches n or L is near n?

## Why This Is Asked
Tests practical dynamic graph reasoning, not pure theory. It probes how a candidate handles batch updates, cycle detection, and trade-offs between incremental updates and full recomputation in large graphs similar to social graphs or dependency graphs.

## Key Concepts
- Dynamic graphs, reachability, cycle detection
- Topological order maintenance, SCCs
- Amortized analysis, batch processing, cache locality

## Code Example
```python
# skeleton for batch update
def batch_update(edges, order, has_cycle):
    for u,v in edges:
        add_edge(u,v)
        if creates_cycle(u,v,order):
            has_cycle = True
            # stop if you only need existence
    return has_cycle
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would deletions of edges affect your approach?
- How would you handle multiple disconnected components improving early-exit checks?

- Distance transform, multi-source BFS, incremental updates, lazy rebuild, grid pruning.

## Code Example

```python
def update_batch(drivers_new_pos):
  for d, pos in drivers_new_pos:
    if dist[pos] > 0:
      dist[pos] = 0
      queue.put(pos)
      while not queue.empty():
        x,y = queue.pop()
        for nx,ny in neighbors(x,y):
          if dist[nx][ny] > dist[x][y] + 1:
            dist[nx][ny] = dist[x][y] + 1
            queue.put((nx,ny))
```
